title: [recoverability] no commit built on the history before a rewrite is ever pushed: the rewrite guard reads a commit's whole history (incrementally, against the commits proven clean), and the integrator names such a stale checkpoint once
prompt:
Spawn, objective 194 [recoverability] (after 177; the lead and lead-mac, 2026-11-15: "the last hole of the rewrite"): no commit built on the history before a rewrite is ever pushed, and its task is told so once.

Base: live main 53a3be15 (the rewritten history).

The problem (sync/queue.md, the lead's 02:38 step-12 audit): after the rewrite, the integrator's mirror (ws/.sources/spawn-*.git) still held the old history on its refs, the resident's branch included. The resident's next checkpoint, task 402's 1f9ef20a, was a NEW commit on it (it contains old main 68de4b6c). 177's guard, rewrite_guard::why_old, refuses a recorded id the commit map names as changed or dropped, and a commit whose history OUTSIDE every ref of the mirror holds one (`rev-list C --not --all`). 1f9ef20a is in no map, and the mirror's own refs reached all of its old history, so the guard passed it. The integrator's re-push of the lost checkpoint was then refused by git as non-fast-forward (nothing old reached spawn.git), and every pass recorded the task `stale`, "the pushed branch (...) does not contain the report's checkpoint (...)". A filter on `--not --all` cannot fix it: a ref on a new commit built on old history (1f9ef20a itself) taints the --not set the same way.

Read first: crates/spawn-cli/src/rewrite_guard.rs (why_old, refused); crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs (pushed_candidate, push_again, name_unknown, Judge::judge).

What changes:
(1) why_old's third check reads the commit's whole history: a commit whose history holds any commit the map names as changed or dropped (`commit_map_olds`: new is distinct from old; one the rewrite kept is not old) is refused, whatever ref holds it: "the commit C is built on the history before the rewrite: N commit(s) of its history were changed or dropped by it (the first: X)". A walk of the whole history is the only exact form when a rewrite keeps some ids: a check of the roots, or a merge-base with old main, misses old history above a kept commit.
(2) The walk is incremental (the lead's change to the design): per repository (git dir), the last 64 commits proven clean bound every walk, `git rev-list C --not <clean...>` (a clean commit's whole history is clean), so a new checkpoint walks only its own new commits; the last 64 proven old are kept with their reason, and a commit proven before (clean or old) is answered without a walk. The map's changed or dropped set is read once per repository and process (the map is insert-once). Commits never change, so a proof holds for the process's life. A clean commit the repository lost since (a gc) fails the walk: the walk is made again from nothing and the clean proofs start over.
(3) The integrator, on a stale verdict (pushed_candidate), asks why_old of the report's checkpoint, else the latest: one refused (but not "an unknown commit", which name_unknown says as before) makes the verdict "the report's|latest checkpoint is from before the rewrite: <why_old's reason>". Nothing is pushed again: push_again already asks why_old, and records the rewrite_refused alert once (writer push-again).
(4) That stale verdict is recorded once in the integrator's life (the lead's ruling): the integrator keeps the (task, revision, reason) it recorded and records the same one no more. A restart, each deploy's included, records it once more; no polled read is added for it.

What stays: every other verdict and its record; the other writers' guards (set-aside, fork) answer as before, through the same why_old; with no map loaded nothing is refused.

Polled reads and their cost: why_old is asked on the stale path only (a task whose pushed branch lags its checkpoint), and by the three writers, as before. Its walk, timed read-only on the live integrator mirror (ws/.sources/spawn-b7fb2686353ed291.git, 337 refs; p194time.sh), at live main 007563ed:
- cold (no proof yet: the whole history): 4,175 commits, 38-69 ms (5 runs);
- incremental (main against its parent, as a new checkpoint against the clean one before it): 1 commit, 2-4 ms.
A commit on old history walks the old history once (about 4.9k commits, the cold cost), then is answered from its proof. The map's changed or dropped set (about 4,913 ids) is read once per process: select old from spawn_commit_map where new is distinct from old.

Tests:
- rewrite_guard::tests::a_commit_built_on_the_old_history_is_refused_whatever_ref_holds_it_walked_once (new): with the mirror's refs on the old history and on the resident's old-history checkpoint, the checkpoint is refused with its reason and a commit on the new history is not; in a repository of its own, a first walk covers the whole history (4), a child of a clean commit walks itself alone (1), a commit proven once walks nothing (0), and an old-history commit walks only what the clean proofs do not reach (3), then nothing.
- rewrite_guard::tests::a_commit_is_refused_when_it_or_its_unreferenced_history_is_from_before_the_rewrite: its on-old-history case now reads the new reason (the same count and first commit).
No test is renamed or dropped.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/rewrite_guard.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs. The owner's (194-owner.diff): rsi/scenarios/194.sh (new).
Size: fleet +256 -16: rewrite_guard.rs +221 -16 (code about 110, the new test about 110), integrate.rs +51 (code). Owner: 194.sh 386. Code about 160, under the bar.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/194.sh, black box through `spawn resident propose/approve`, `spawn task assign`, `spawn commit-map load` and `spawn integrate`, on a source it rewrites as filter-repo would (m0 kept, m1 rewritten to m1', the resident's work W on m1 to W'); the old objects stay in the source and in the integrator's mirror, where the resident's branch is W. After the map is loaded the resident commits C on W in the mirror (a new id), its checkpoint, and reports C. A second mission on the same source has a worker's work N on the new main, its checkpoint and report. One integrator runs, as on the host (passes 300 ms apart), until it has judged the resident's task three times and N has landed:
(1) the resident's task has exactly one `stale` verdict, which says C "is built on the history before the rewrite"; its spawn/<agent> in the source is still W'; no ref of the source reaches C, W or m1; one rewrite_refused alert names push-again, the task and C.
(2) N lands: main holds its file and nothing from before the rewrite (the guard does not refuse the new history).
On the base (53a3be15) 194.sh exits 1: "(1) stale verdicts of the resident's task in 3 passes of one integrator (its last: {"verdict":"stale","reason":"the pushed branch (...) does not contain the report's checkpoint (...)"}): expected [1], got [2]", "(1) the stale verdict does not say C is built on the history before the rewrite: the pushed branch (...) does not contain the report's checkpoint (...)", "(1) rewrite_refused alerts naming push-again, task 1 and C: expected [1], got [0]".

Proof (rev-b, sync/obj-194/194-proof.txt): at o194 2bd4fd36 on 53a3be15 (194-throwaway.diff is exactly its diff). Run D (05:31): 194.sh fails on the base with the three lines above and passes twice on the fix; the unit tests (rewrite_guard, name_unknown: 2), the store tests (commit_map: 4), spawn-core's lib (89), fmt and clippy pass; the kept 177.sh passes; test lists 1669 -> 1670, 0 missing, 1 new. Run E (06:43) repeated all of it with the same results.
7 mutants (mut194.py), each alone, each its own binary, all killed:
- by 194.sh and a unit test: ancestry-ignored;
- by 194.sh alone: stale-not-named, said-every-pass (each "(1) stale verdicts ... expected [1]");
- by the new unit test alone (the walk counts and the kept proofs; the scenario's answers stay right, only slower): walk-unbounded, proof-not-read, old-not-kept;
- by the kept 177.sh alone (Run F, 06:58): unknown-as-old, at 177's (2), "the stale verdict does not name the unknown commit: the report's checkpoint is from before the rewrite: the commit 1111... is an unknown commit". The gate runs 177.sh on every candidate.
The polled cost above is from p194time.sh (read-only, the live mirror). Every line is in 194-proof.txt.

Verified by: the gate runs 194.sh on the candidate. After landing, a checkpoint built on the old history (as task 402's) reads "built on the history before the rewrite" once, with one rewrite_refused alert, and nothing is pushed. rev-g reviews.
